subject: Best practice for integrating d3 with fine-tuned control in Shiny?

messages.author: bda90bcea347c4f0
messages.subject: Best practice for integrating d3 with fine-tuned control in Shiny?
parts:
Hello,

I'm a huge fan of rCharts and networkD3 in order to generate d3 charts in Shiny. However, if I need to add more control such as hover details, expanding nodes by clicking a row in a data.table, I'm not sure what the best way to go about this is. 

I know you can write the entire ui.R file in HTML, but is that ideal? Any suggestions on how I can best utilize my R skills and a javascript/d3 developer would be appreciated.

Thank you

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Best practice for integrating d3 with fine-tuned control in Shiny?
parts:
You might be able to do this with callback functions, using the htmlwidgets::onRender function--see the reference documentation of that function for more details.

library(networkD3)
data(MisLinks, MisNodes)
forceNetwork(Links = MisLinks, Nodes = MisNodes, Source = "source",
             Target = "target", Value = "value", NodeID = "name",
             Group = "group", opacity = 0.4) %>%
  onRender("function(el, x) {
    ...
  }")

The value of "x" in the JS code is highly dependent on the htmlwidget binding code; in the case of the networkD3::forceNetwork function, it's the d3.layout.force() object.

With the GitHub version of htmlwidgets (i.e. not yet released on CRAN) you can pass an additional argument such as a list or data frame to onRender, and that will be made available to your JS code as well.
